record.title: The even-base min-entropy formula conjecture for entropoid power shapes
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{E}_{p^2}$ be an entropoid and let $g\in\mathbb{E}^*_{(p-1)^2}$ generate its maximal multiplicative subgroupoid. For every even base $\mathfrak{b}=2b_1<b_{\max}$, let $n(\mathfrak{b},i)=\max n_{ij}$. The **even-base min-entropy conjecture.**

$$
n(\mathfrak{b},i)=(\mathfrak{b}-1)\left((\mathfrak{b}-1)^{i-1}-(\mathfrak{b}-2)^{i-1}\right),
$$

and consequently

$$
H_{\infty}(\xi_i)=1-\left(\frac{\mathfrak{b}-2}{\mathfrak{b}-1}\right)^{i-1}.
$$

The formula formalizes the observed even-versus-odd base pattern in the distribution of bracketing shapes; the paper reports it as an observed conjectural relation rather than proving it.

record.title: The DEDHP hardness conjecture in Sylow q-subquasigroups
record.statement: Let $\mathbb{E}_{p^2}$ be an entropoid with $p=2q+1$ a safe prime, and let $g_q$ generate its Sylow $q$-subquasigroup $\mathbb{E}^*_{q^2}$. The **Sylow DEDHP hardness conjecture.** No algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ solves DEDHP in $\mathbb{E}^*_{q^2}$ with significantly greater advantage than uniformly random guessing. The claim is presented as a plausible cryptographic conjecture after showing that DEDHP is efficiently solvable in the maximal quasigroup; no resolution is given.

record.title: The computational discrete entropoid root hardness conjecture
record.review_depth: Source Conjecture5 and discussion of CDERP root-index model
record.literal_statement:
Let $\mathbb{E}_{p^2}$ be an entropoid, with $p=2q+1$ a safe prime having $\lambda$ bits, and let $g$ generate $\mathbb{E}^*_{(p-1)^2}$. Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an algorithm for CDERP. The **CDERP hardness conjecture.** Over uniformly chosen $(\mathbf{B},\mathfrak{b})\xleftarrow{\mathbf{r}}\mathbb{L}$, the probability that

$$
\mathcal{A}\left(x^{(\mathbf{B},\mathfrak{b})},(\mathbf{B},\mathfrak{b})\right)=x
$$

is $\mathtt{negl}(\lambda)$. This conjectures the computational difficulty of extracting non-associative entropoid roots; the paper gives no proof or resolution.
